label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
# A letter from Thandi, for everyone who has been checking in

To my friends, neighbours, the Little Acorns families, and everyone else who has messaged, called or asked after me:

I’m safe. I’m staying at my sister’s place in Rondebosch, and Marmalade is safe too.

My phone has been going mad since Saturday, and I’m so tired that the thought of answering everyone one by one feels impossible right now. Please don’t take that as me being ungrateful. It’s the opposite, honestly. I’ve cried at so many of your messages. I just don’t have the energy to keep repeating everything, so I’m putting it all in one letter. Please feel free to forward it to anyone who has been worried about me.

**What happened**

At about 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November, a fire started in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Obs. It wasn’t my flat. Mine is flat 12, on the second floor.

There are 14 flats in the building. Everyone got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and were sent home afterwards, which is an enormous relief.

The fire department says it was probably an electrical fault, but they are still investigating. I don’t want to guess beyond that or add to any rumours.

The only reason I woke up was because my neighbour, Uncle Faizel, went banging on every door on our floor in his vest and slippers. That is how I found out there was a fire. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade and got out. Nothing else.

Marmalade then disappeared under a car for two hours afterwards, which was exactly the extra thing my nerves needed. But she is here, she is fine, and she is with me.

My flat is basically gone. There is smoke and water damage everywhere, and the ceiling came down in the lounge. The landlord says nobody is going back in for at least six weeks. I don’t want to go through every detail of that night, or list every single thing I’ve lost. I know people are asking because they care, but I’d rather not relive it all again and again.

Furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can’t. That’s where I’m keeping my head at the moment.

**What I actually need**

I hate asking for help. I really do. But there are a few things that would make a genuine difference:

- **Help with the deposit for a new place.** This is the biggest thing worrying me at the moment. I need to find somewhere else to live and start putting a home together again.
- **Shoes and clothes for work.** I need shoes I can wear to school, size 6, and work clothes, size 34.
- **A laptop, if anyone has an old one that still works.** All my lesson planning was on mine. It doesn’t need to be fancy or new — just something reliable that I can work on.

If you have something specific to offer, please put the details in one message so I can come back to it when I have the headspace. I might not answer immediately, but I’m not ignoring you.

**What I don’t need**

Please, no more general clothes. People have been incredibly generous, and I already have more than enough. I’ll pass the extras on to people in the other flats.

We also don’t need food. My sister’s freezer is genuinely full.

I’m saying this only because I want people’s kindness and money to go where it will actually help. Please don’t think for a second that I’m not grateful for every single offer.

**The fundraiser Zinhle has set up**

Zinhle has set up a BackaBuddy page for me:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**. When I checked this morning, it was already at **R11 400**. I honestly don’t know how to put into words what it feels like to see so many people helping, including people I don’t even know well.

The money will help me get back on my feet, particularly with a deposit for somewhere new to live and the essential things I need to replace.

I felt very strange about having a fundraiser at all. I kept saying there must be other people who need help more, and that I could somehow manage by myself. Zinhle eventually told me to shut up and accept it. So that is what I’m trying to do.

If you’re able to donate, thank you. Please don’t feel any pressure if you can’t. Sharing the correct link is also a help, and so are all the messages and practical offers people have already sent.

**An important warning about another “fund”**

There is another page calling itself **“Thandi Fire Relief”** on a different site, as well as a WhatsApp message asking people to EFT money into a Capitec account.

**That is not me. It is not connected to me, Zinhle or our fundraiser.**

I have reported it. Please don’t pay money into that account, and please don’t forward that WhatsApp as though it came from me.

The only fundraiser I recognise is Zinhle’s BackaBuddy page at the link above. If you have already shared the other one, please send a correction so people don’t accidentally donate to the wrong place. I feel awful having to include this in a letter about people’s generosity, but I also don’t want anyone being taken advantage of.

**For my Little Acorns families**

For those who don’t know me personally, I teach the Ladybirds at Little Acorns Pre-Primary in Mowbray — Grade 00, my lovely class of four- and five-year-olds.

To the parents: **the end-of-year concert on 27 November is still happening. Please don’t worry. The Ladybirds will have crowns.**

I had taken all the concert things home to laminate. The 22 crowns are gone, and so is the children’s handprint banner. Of everything in the flat, that one got me especially badly. It was only paper, paint and the children’s small handprints, but you can understand why.

We’ll make a plan. We’ll make new crowns. We are pre-primary teachers — cardboard, glue and making a plan are basically our whole personalities.

I’ll be back at school on Wednesday. I know everyone will be concerned, but please don’t make a big thing of the fire in front of the children. The kindest thing you can do for me is help keep their school day feeling as normal as possible. They need their teacher, their routine and their friends. I need a bit of that normality too.

**Thank you**

There have been so many acts of kindness that I can’t fit them all in, but I keep thinking about the school mom who dropped a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday. She didn’t even knock or wait to be thanked. She just left it there because she thought I might need it.

To her, to Uncle Faizel, to Zinhle, to my sister, to my neighbours, to everyone at Little Acorns, and to every person who has sent a message or done something practical: thank you. I have been completely overwhelmed by people’s goodness. Sometimes in a nice way, sometimes in a “now I’m crying again” way.

I will get back to people slowly. Please don’t be offended if I don’t answer DMs, miss a call, or take days to reply to something kind you’ve written. I’m not keeping a scorecard of who has replied to whom. I’m just trying to sleep, deal with one thing at a time, and get myself upright again.

For now, I am safe, Marmalade is safe, I have a bed at my sister’s, and I know I’m not facing this alone. That is more than enough to hold on to today.

Thank you for reading this, and thank you for caring.

With so much gratitude,  
**Thandi**
